I will keep my land in the wheat-maize rotation. In Quzhou County, that is the most dependable way for me to use the full year, match the local climate, and make use of machinery and irrigation that I already understand well. At my age, I value a system that is stable, efficient, and not too labor-intensive, so I will avoid scattered small experiments and focus on two main grain crops with predictable management.

For the current spring, I will carry my winter wheat through to harvest first. I will manage it with moderate but not excessive fertilizer, three irrigations if water is available at the key stages, and a few targeted pesticide sprays only when disease or insects justify them. After wheat harvest, I will move quickly into summer maize. I will use hybrid maize because the yield is more reliable for me, plant it immediately after wheat to avoid losing moisture and growing days, and use no-tillage or very light disturbance so I can save time and keep the soil structure in decent shape. Overall, I am choosing a practical, high-yield, lower-risk plan rather than a complicated one.
